title: The "Storm" Speech
subtitle: At the very least, we all now have a better understanding of how home appliances work.

trails.title: Encrypted Record #832
trails.description: After a monotonous, constant noise, a response comes from the other end of the line.

content.text:
"Regarding Zeno's request for assistance in establishing a dedicated communication line with the Timekeeper, we hope to understand the details."

"The exact content of the communication is a military secret. I cannot divulge the details."

"The Scientific Computing Center needs to understand the purpose of Zeno's establishment of communication to judge whether it is worth diverting manpower to build a dedicated line."

"Zeno's purpose is a military secret. I cannot divulge the details."

" ... Next, I will ask some simple questions. If you continue to answer with 'I cannot divulge the details,' I will take it as a sign of admission. Do you understand?"

"I am not authorized to answer that question."

" ... Very well, then is Zeno preparing for a military operation against the Manus Vindictae and therefore needs to establish communication with the Timekeeper for this purpose?"

"I cannot divulge the details."

"Good, this operation will ensure the Timekeeper's safety then, won't it?"

"I cannot divulge the details."

"This is an unconventional operation, isn't it?"

"I cannot divulge the details."

"This operation was most likely inspired by the Pax Security Council, correct?"

"We are soldiers. Soldiers act on orders, miss."

*Zeno then hung up the call.

items.text: The "Storm" Speech

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: We don't have time. I'll spare you the technicalities and explain it straight.
He pops off the marker cap and draws a few lines on the board, exuding confidence with every stroke.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Our biggest problem is the limit of the bloodline. Low-rank arcanists can't command high-rank arcane rituals, similar to how household appliances can't withstand what's beyond their designated voltage.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: In most cases, the caster can only use their own arcane circuits that run through their inherited bloodline.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But what if the caster were in a special electric field? What if we used existing circuits on the outside and put the caster into a greater circuit?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What if we factored in the entire planet and used the atmosphere to split the current flowing through us, by adding more appliances to the circuit?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Don't be ridiculous, Adler! We are not household appliances!
The ferrofluid frowns, questioning the premises of Enigma's proposal.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Hold on. Let me finish.
Lucy listens without a word, giving him some courage to go on.
He draws a big circle next to the little person on the board.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: 24 hours before the "Storm," the entire world is charged with abundant arcane energy. It becomes a space emanating pneuma, a cloud ready to discharge—a special electric field.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Look at "asymmetrical nuclide R," the key to the "Storm" immunity, was inside the "Storm" all along.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And look at how the Mandragora is the antidote to its own poison—the solution can be hidden in the question itself.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The arcane energy a caster inherently lacks can be borrowed from the surroundings during the "Storm." We just need a way to induct that energy.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And Laplace happens to have all the data for the calculations. The observation systems we've built over the past eight years have not been in vain!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: First, we derive a formula to determine the pneuma needed from the "Storm" based on the arcanist's lineage.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Then, we'll design a converter to transform the external pneuma into what they can use—they will no longer be bound by their limits!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: With just one calculation and one conversion, we can turn anyone into a capable caster.
He excitedly stretches out his arms and ends his epic monologue.
It is a good thing that emotions cannot be read on an Awakened being's face.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: I knew I shouldn't have wasted my time listening to you. What are you saying, Adler?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: You made up a confusing story, then drew conclusions from it.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The second part is purely theoretical, I admit. But the basis of my theory is correct, and I have read Medicine Pocket's paper.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: But arcanum is not electricity! You're too caught up in your excitement to remember the basics. You know nothing about arcanum.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: It's still a form of energy, yes? No one here knows what the "Storm" is, but we do know that it's a massive arcane energy field. We can harness it, much like arcanists use arrays to amplify their incantations.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I see what Researcher Adler is trying to say. A creative solution indeed.
The director gets up from her chair and intervenes.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: But ma'am ...

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Do not worry, Ulrich. I also have noticed that humans could be smart and stupid at the same time. Perhaps that is why they need to have their work peer-reviewed.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Uh, than ... ks ...?
She nods amicably, pleased that her recently improved interpersonal skills have come in handy.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There is a type of electrophotography invented by Semyon Kirlian and his wife Valentina Kirlian in 1939. That depicts the energy field surrounding an object or body.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It was later used by Laplace as a method of measuring arcane power, notably for the "Storm" observation systems.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Through it, we are able to capture and measure the arcane "light" or "aura" that is invisible to the naked eye.
Wasting no more time on mediation, the robot comes to a conclusion.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The plan of Researcher Adler is feasible. Laplace also has the technology to support it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We have the "Storm" observation stations, the capable casters, and the best mathematicians.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Ulrich, please ask Ms. Titor to lead the calculations, then experiment outside the safe zone and record the Pneuma Constant needed for casting the incantation.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And do not give the incantation to anyone. I doubt they can resist trying it.
Ulrich lets out a reluctant hum and leaves the room as instructed.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Simone, please contact Researcher X. His "Balancing Helmet" could be the prototype for our converter.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: That helmet balances the energy field in and out of our bodies, and was once used to protect researchers working with dangerous arcane skills. We could boost its power and use it as a substitute for Adler's converter.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But we should postpone their testing request until we have completed our experiments on the side effects.
Her assistant gives a quick nod and begins drafting the notice.
The tasks are quickly assigned to the right people in less than a minute.
Only one person seems to have been left out.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What about me, ma'am? Should I go with the calculations team or help with the converter?
He takes a tentative step forward, curious about his role in this endeavor.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Right. I wanted to talk about that.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You have proven to us the value of human thoughts and perspectives. I am glad that your struggles with the bottle did not damage your brain, Adler.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am confident that your discoveries will save many lives in the "Storm" once implemented.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The bottle? But it's been seven years ...
She just keeps on smiling.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But you overlooked one thing in your plan.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What about your people, the humans, who can never cast incantations?
An apt question.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: They were not included in the plan. I just came up with something that took the least steps to reach the desired outcome.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: To save humans, they'll have to rely on equipment. Only when we have better control over the ritual can we store it on arcane devices for mass production.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Then you should go perfect it.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: We only have 16 hours and 30 minutes until the "Storm"! There's not enough time to ...

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The feasible part of your plan is in motion, and all of Laplace will provide the help we need. We will make it work.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: As for yourself, perfect your plan so we can save everyone, including the humans.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And we only have 16 hours and 30 minutes to find the solution.
The directions are given—clear, precise, with no room for ambiguity.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Understood. I will think of something.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You're right about this one.
He turns and walks away with long, purposeful strides.
Behind Lucy, Simone has finished drafting.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: There was no way he "overlooked" his own race.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Yet, he still gave up his own people and brought this plan to us.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Were we too hard on him?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Were we?
She turns nonchalantly and sits back in her chair.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But I made the right decision.
The internal line rings.
The assistant puts down the list of side effects and grabs the phone.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Yes? Yes. We will provide the tech support.
She ends the call with a grave expression on her face.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: It was Zeno, ma'am.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: They lost contact with Team Timekeeper three hours ago. They're asking us for tech support.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: They have to make contact with the island immediately.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: ... Urrm ...
The mind sinks and floats in an ocean of lethargy.
A piece of driftwood would be well timed.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Don't worry, Sophia. It is just a game!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I won't be in there for long. You can wait for me on the beach if you want. Okay?
The wood dissolves into foam.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: No, 37, don't!
She wakes up on a cold piece of rock.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: ... Where ... What happened?
TO BE CONTINUED…
